body.p: Applicant notes with appreciation the allowance of claims 1-2, 10-11 and 23 and the indication of allowable subject matter in claims 3-9 and 14-22. In the outstanding office action, claims 3-4, 6, 8, and 21-23 were objected to and claims 3-9 and 14-22 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112.

While Applicant respectfully traverses the above rejections, in the interest of expediting the prosecution of the present application without adversely affecting Applicant's rights to pursue the previously presented claims in a divisional or continuation application, Applicant has amended the claims as shown above.

Concerning the objection to the claims and the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 112, Applicant has amended the claims as indicated above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the objections to claims and the rejections under 35 U.S.C. §112.
Applicant notes that the below objection in claim 3 cannot be found and Applicant presumes this is a typographical error in the outstanding office action.
Claims 3-4, 6, 8 and 21-23 are objected to because of the following informalities:
" Claim 3 line 8 reads "be at least", --by the at least-- is suggested.
In addition, Applicant presumes the below objection refers to claim 9 as similar text is found claim 8.
* Claim 8 line 2 reads "III", --IV-- is suggested.

Concerning the objection to claim 6 as being a substantial duplicate of claim 4, Applicant notes that claim 4 requires "a type II tendon sheath constraint element" and claim 6 requires "a type III tendon sheath constraint element". The application, as filed, describes the type II and type III tendon sheath constraint elements in at least paragraphs

[0020] The type II tendon sheath constraint element is a flexible element, and comprises one or more second guide grooves or second guide holes to guide at least five of the compound tendon sheaths or the single-layer tendon sheaths to slide along their respective axes, and a second structure allowing one or more of the compound tendon sheaths or the single-layer tendon sheaths to respectively curl inside the type II tendon sheath constraint element, wherein the type II tendon sheath constraint element is arranged to be installed at wrist joint of the dexterous hand, or ankle joint of the bionic mechanical foot, or the other robotic joints that are passed/bypassed by at least five of the compound tendon
sheaths or the singlc-laycr tendon sheaths.

[0021] The type III tendon sheath constraint element is used to restrain the position and deformation range of one or more compound tendon sheaths or single-layer tendon sheaths through the bar part (non-hinge part) of the robot joint, and provide a certain cushion space allowing curvature for each compound tendon sheath or single-layer tendon sheath, especially suitable for installation on the palm of a
dexterous hand.
[0022] The type III tendon sheath constraint element com- prises one or more third guide grooves or third guide holes

to guide one or more of the compound tendon sheaths or the single-layer tendon sheaths to slide along their respective axes, and a third structure allowing one or more of the compound tendon sheaths or the single-layer tendon sheaths to respectively curl inside the type III tendon sheath con- straint element, wherein the type III tendon sheath constraint element is arranged to be installed at palm part or metacarpal of the dexterous hand, or foot part of the bionic mechanical
foot, or non-joint parts of other robotic mechanisms.
As such, there clearly is a difference between "a type II tendon sheath constraint
element" and "a type III tendon sheath constraint element". Thus, Applicant respectfully
requests the objection with regard to claim 6 be withdrawn.
Concerning the below rejections of claims 3, 5, 7 and 8, Applicant respectfully
submits that each of these claims refer to "first guide grooves or guide holes", "second

guide grooves or guide holes", "third guide grooves or guide holes", and "fourth guide grooves or guide holes" respectively as opposed to "guide grooves and guide holes". As such, Applicant respectfully submits these claims are indeed definite.
- Claim 3 lines 3-4 recite the limitation "one or more first guide g rooves or first guide holes". I is
unclearif this limitation is referring to the guide grooves and g uide holes recited in claim 1, or
if this limitation requires additional guide grooves and guide holes.
" Claim 5 lines 3-4 recite the limitation "one or more second guide grooves or second guide
holes". It is unclearif this limitation is referring to the guide grooves and guide holes recited in
claim 1, or if this limitation requires additional guide grooves and guide holes.
" Claim 7 line 3 recites the limitation "one or more third guide grooves orthird guide holes". It is
unclear if this limitation is referring to the guide grooves and glide holes recited in claim 1, or
if this limitation requires additional guide grooves and guide holes.
" Claim 8 lines 4-5 recite the limitation "one or more fourth guide grooves or fourth guide holes".
It is unclear if this limitation is referring to the guide grooves and guide holes recited in claim 1,
or if this limitation requires additional guide grooves and guide holes.
Concerning the below rejection of claim 3.
" Claim 3 lines 4 and 9 recite the limitation "the single layertendon sheaths". There is insufficient
antecedent basis for this limitation in the claim.
Applicant respectfully submits that claim 3 previously recited "single layer tendon sheaths". As such, claim 3 is believed to be definite and no further amendments are necessary.
In view of the above comments and amendments, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the objections to the claims and the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 112.

Amendments to, cancellation of, and additions to, the claims, as set forth herein, are made in order to streamline prosecution in this case by limiting examination and argument to certain claimed embodiments. Amendment or cancellation of the claims is not in any manner intended to, and should not be construed to, waive Applicant's right in the future to seek such unamended or cancelled subject matter, or similar matter (whether in equivalent, broader, or narrower form) in the present application, and any continuation, divisional, continuation-in-part, RCE, or any other application claiming priority to or through the present application, nor in any manner to indicate an intention, expressed or implied, to surrender any equivalent to the claims as pending after such amendments or cancellations.
In view of the above amendments and the discussion relating thereto, it is

respectfully submitted that the present application is in condition for allowance. Such action is most earnestly solicited.
